name: Sargon of Akkad
contribution: The founder of the Akkadian Empire, known for his conquests of the Sumerian city-states, around 2300 BC.

checks.lead: Sargon of Akkad (; Akkadian: 𒊬𒊒𒄀, romanized: Šarrugi; died c. 2279 BC), also known as Sargon the Great, was the founder of the Akkadian Empire (also labelled 'Sargonic', after him), known for his conquests of the Sumerian city-states, around 2300 BC. He is sometimes identified as the first person in recorded history to rule over an empire. The dates of his reign, which are uncertain, are often estimated to be between 2334 and 2279 BC, but a more recent proposal places it in the period from 2316 to 2277 BC.
